sealed_ledger.meaning: every sealed number is what the frozen rule produces from results strictly earlier than the moment it was recorded - i.e. the seal can be audited without trusting it

prospective_resolution.scoring: Brier and log loss on the home-win indicator; ties score 0.5; benchmarks are the 0.50 coin and the frozen 0.55 home baseline. Skill is benchmark-relative by construction: 1 - model/0.55-baseline.
prospective_resolution.why_it_matters: This is the only part of PR-01 that was not chosen after seeing data: the prediction was written, hashed and committed before kickoff. It is also the smallest sample in the repository, and it is labelled as such.
prospective_resolution.honesty: n = 1 resolved. One game is one game: there is no interval here, no ranking, and no claim about skill in either direction. A resolved prospective record becomes evidence only when it is wide enough to survive the game-cluster bootstrap, which needs >=100 games (PR-01 promotion clause).

sealing_cadence.rule: seal week W in the window that opens once week W-1's last game is final and closes at week W's first kickoff. Today the Week 11 slate is fully sealed, so there is nothing to write; sealing Week 12 must wait for Week 11's final result. A build that sealed Week 12 now would use ratings that are one week stale, and would say so in the row's clock time.
sealing_cadence.next_window: opens after the last final of the current slate; closes at the next slate's first kickoff (both printed by the official by-week pages, not by this tool)

blank_by_policy.market_line: no official price source in this repository - open question Q-02
blank_by_policy.residual: residual = fair - market, so it is blank while the market line is blank
blank_by_policy.roi_staking: no prices means no settlement; see the demotion gate and G5
blank_by_policy.total_fair_line: the model is a margin model; its total is the league-average total, published as a floor and labelled as one, not as an estimate of the total

limits: n = 118 games, one season, one conference-independent sample; the interval, not the point estimate, is the result
the model has no personnel, availability, rest or venue feature - it is the baseline those features have to beat, not a proposal
ratings use points scored and allowed vs whoever; schedule strength is not adjusted, so BUF's and NYJ's ratings are not comparable in the way an opponent-adjusted model's would be
one season cannot test calibration at the tails; the 0.8-1.0 bin is printed with its count
